newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends flat, data within expectations.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends flat, data within expectations.

text.p: The key March three-month euroyen interest rate futures contract settled unchanged on Friday as early gains were erased after economic data released in the afternoon came within expectations.
"Those who bought in the morning sold on the fact, when the economic data was released," said a city bank dealer.
Trade was subdued in the midst of the summer holiday season.

Tokyo July department store sales fell 5.7 percent in July compared with a year earlier. Japan's trade ministry said it expected July-September industrial output to rise 0.2 percent from the previous quarter. This compares with the ministry's previous forecast of a 0.3 percent rise.

The March contract's rise in the morning was also attributed to a sharp price rise in yen bonds. The yield of key 182nd 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) briefly fell to an all-time low of 2.065 percent.
But selling on the topside capped the contract at 99.26, equal to Thursday's high, traders said.
"If the contract breaks above a resistance point at 99.26-99.27, its next target will be 99.30," said another city bank dealer.
The March may remain upward biased next week, backed by short-covering ahead of a shift in the benchmark status to the June expected later this month at earliest.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) conducted a neutral operation on Friday, which traders said was as expected since it is the last day of the current bank reserve reporting period.
The key overnight call rate fell to around 0.44 percent from Thursday's weighted average of 0.45 percent.
When the new bank reserve period starts on Monday, the key overnight call rate is seen stabilising at the higher end of the 0.40-0.50 percent range, traders said.
The BOJ tries to keep the call rate below the discount rate, which is 0.50 percent.

"Upward pressure in overnight call rates seem weaker than a month ago as long-term CDs have been constantly issued," said a trust bank dealer. About 40 billion yen of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.58 percent, unchanged from Thursday. "The CD rate seems to have hit a short-term bottom," said another dealer. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk
